newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Human rights court finds against Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Human rights court finds against Colombia.

text.p: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights on Monday ordered the Colombian government to pay $89,500 to the families of two people who disappeared in Colombia in February 1989.
The court ordered the payment to be made within one year to the families of Isidro Caballero Delgado, 32, and Maria del Carmen Santana, 19, who disappeared near the town of Guaduas.

The Inter-American Human Rights Commission brought the case in December 1994 and the court found a year later that Colombia's government was responsible for the disappearances due to the involvement of members of its armed forces.
"The Colombian State is obliged to continue in its efforts to locate the remains of the victims and hand them over to their families," the ruling said.
